correctness.rationale: The stationary initial distribution P(+)= (a+epsilon)/(2a) is explicitly matched to the two-by-two Feynman-Kac tilted generator. Diagonalizing gives F=e^(-at)[cosh(zt)+(b/z)sinh(zt)], z²=a²-v²+2iv epsilon, b=a+iv epsilon/a. With epsilon≠0 and z=u+iw, u>0, the identity Re(b conjugate z)=u(a+w²/a)>0 yields |b-z|<|b+z|; any positive-time root would require e^(2zt)=(b-z)/(b+z), impossible by modulus. For epsilon=0, the overdamped/critical formulas stay positive, and the v>a sinusoid gives all listed simple zero times. The squared modulus derivative is a positive scalar times R cos(2wt+theta)-A(t), where A(t)=(a-u)P e^(2ut)+(a+u)Q e^(-2ut)>0 is strictly convex and tends to infinity. On each positive cosine lobe the sign function is strictly concave, so at most one increasing-modulus component. For v>a as epsilon→0, u~(v/omega)|epsilon|, w→omega, and A(t)/R→(a/v)cosh(2ut) uniformly for bounded scaled times. The unique envelope threshold gives a lobe count asymptotic and coefficient omega² arcosh(v/a)/(2 pi v). Analytic parity of |F|² and the simple symmetric zeros give minimum time shifts O_j(epsilon²) and depth O_j(|epsilon|³) after its exact linear coefficient. Independent scipy matrix exponential vs closed form agreed to <3e-12 for four cases; independent concave-lobe counts at a=1,v=2 checked representative asymmetries (epsilon=0.1 ->3 and 0.01 ->31). These finite numerics do not prove the zero-free or asymptotic statements.
residual_risks: The asymptotic is at fixed v>a and stationary initialization, not uniform near v=a or for other noise channels.
The nonzero asymmetry all-time zero classification uses the exact Markov generator; independent numerical propagation corroborates but cannot certify all t.
The independent floating-point lobe exploration had a roundoff-sized apparent first-lobe positivity at epsilon=.002; no exact count is inferred from this artifact.

value.rationale: Counting connected strict modulus-recovery intervals over all future times is a mathematically natural observable of a physically standard non-Gaussian dephasing model. Arbitrarily small stationary switching-rate asymmetry changes infinitely many exact zeros and revivals to a finite number without zeros; the theorem quantifies that singular crossover with a sharp nonzero rate-dependent 1/|epsilon| coefficient and resolves the local rounding of each formerly dark time. The precise global cutoff and singular count add information not provided by the already-known exact amplitude or qualitative short-time recovery figures.
residual_risks: The result addresses one stationary classical two-state fluctuator, not general noise ensembles, quantum backflow criteria, or critical coupling scaling.

final_claim: For stationary two-state Markov switching +1->-1 at rate a-epsilon, -1->+1 at a+epsilon, a>0, |epsilon|<a and phase strength v>0, the dephasing amplitude F_epsilon(t) has no finite-time zero when epsilon!=0; for epsilon=0 it has positive zeros iff v>a, at the stated t_j. For v>a fixed, the finite number N(epsilon) of increasing-modulus time intervals obeys |epsilon|N(epsilon)->(v^2-a^2) arcosh(v/a)/(2 pi v); each symmetric zero rounds to a unique local minimum of depth [v^2(1+a t_j)e^(-a t_j)/(a(v^2-a^2))]|epsilon|+O_j(|epsilon|^3).
limitations: The exact dephasing amplitude and qualitative asymmetry suppression were already published; these are not claimed original.
Numeric lobe exploration is finite and susceptible to machine-roundoff near t=0; claim proof is analytic.
No uniform simultaneous epsilon→0 and v→a limit, nonstationary initial mixture, or channel-capacity theorem.
Publication blocked by existing operational metadata in two publicly facing JSON files.
